summary: Extend the frozen event-platform capability with a tenant-scoped PostgreSQL transactional outbox, caller-transaction-bound enqueue, immutable canonical event intent, expiring SKIP LOCKED relay leases, retry scheduling, and compare-by-lease publication acknowledgement without claiming cross-system exactly-once delivery.

impacts.evidence: Enqueue verifies the already-bound transaction-local organization/workspace scope, relay claims are explicitly tenant scoped, and forced PostgreSQL RLS remains active for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE with no DELETE policy.
The canonical business event payload remains subject to its source purpose/classification; operational retry metadata stores only bounded machine codes and never raw broker/client error text.
No REST/OpenAPI operation changes; the outbox is an internal persistence and event-publication boundary.
Outbox rows persist the exact Task-007 canonical EventBus envelope and preserve the immutable event ID/body across every publication attempt; no second event envelope is introduced.
No connector SDK surface changes and provider code receives no PostgreSQL/Kafka implementation branch.

Atomic high-risk expand migration 000007 adds nullable canonical envelopes for rolling compatibility, ready/lease/publication metadata, indexes, split RLS policies, mutation guards, and migration history registration.

Cross-tenant enqueue is rejected before insert, lease tokens are cryptographically random opaque values, stale leases cannot acknowledge rows, event bodies are immutable, hard delete is blocked, and arbitrary broker error strings are not persisted.
Outbox records facts from an already-authorized transaction; sensitive-operation approval remains Task 017 and is not bypassed or reimplemented here.

The exact event ID, type, aggregate, tenant, correlation/causation and canonical envelope survive relay retries, providing a deterministic link from committed transaction intent to EventBus publication.

Same-event enqueue is idempotent only for an identical immutable envelope; publication is explicitly at-least-once and crash-after-publish can duplicate the same event ID, preserving Task 009 as the mandatory consumer deduplication boundary.
No webhook delivery surface changes; later webhook workers may consume events after the inbox/idempotency boundary.

Outbox age, available time, attempt count, lease expiry, publication time and bounded failure code are explicit operational metadata suitable for lag/stuck-relay SLOs without logging sensitive client errors.
Migration 000007 is expand-only and backup-gated; rollback disables the new relay binary without deleting committed event intents. Backup/restore rehearsal preserves outbox rows and tenant RLS.

Tests cover same-transaction tenant verification, exact duplicate enqueue, collision rejection, SKIP LOCKED lease SQL, compare-by-lease ack/retry, bounded backoff, cancellation recovery, immutable migration guards, RLS shape, atomic rollback, and backup/restore preservation.
